chunks.subject: AP Physics 1
chunks.title: Q4 Qualitative Quantitative Translation (QQT) — 8 points
chunks.content: AP Physics 1 FRQ 4 is Qualitative Quantitative Translation (QQT), 8 points, scored by lettered sub-points. The QQT task requires connecting qualitative reasoning with quantitative analysis: make a claim, support it with physics principles in words, and back it with a consistent quantitative argument (or vice versa). Q4 topic: buoyancy and density of a block in fluid. Points reward: a correct claim/prediction, qualitative reasoning citing the relevant principle (buoyant force, density comparison), a quantitative expression/derivation, and consistency between the qualitative and quantitative answers. Common failure: a claim without supporting principle; quantitative work that contradicts the qualitative reasoning; missing the density/buoyancy relationship.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 1
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4A, 8/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 8/8 — a correct claim, sound qualitative reasoning (buoyancy/density), a consistent quantitative derivation, and agreement between the qualitative and quantitative arguments. Full-credit model for the QQT task.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 1
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4B, 5/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 5/8 — earned the claim and most qualitative reasoning plus part of the quantitative argument, losing points where the quantitative work was incomplete or inconsistent with the qualitative claim. Illustrates a partially connected qualitative–quantitative response.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 1
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4C, 2/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 2/8 — earned only a couple of sub-points (e.g., a claim or one reasoning step), losing the principle-based reasoning and the quantitative support. Illustrates a response that cannot link qualitative reasoning to quantitative analysis.
